analysis:
Examined the memory-management changes in GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift, KVPoolReclaimer.swift and ProcessMemoryLedger.swift. They add an idle-gated proactive sweep (SweepWindow closed/idle/pressure), a releaseRetained hook that asks engines to drop retained free KV segments, a shortfall-signalling flag for direct-charge refusals, and a ProcessMemoryLedger.capacityShortfall computation.

No network, authentication, attestation, key, or ciphertext-handling paths are touched. Per-request reservation logic (reserve/release/resizeReservationBytes/commit) is unchanged in behavior. The reclaimer still revalidates isReclaimAllowed before the GPU callback (KVPoolReclaimer.swift:233 and 241). The rate-limit window is now set only after a flush actually runs (line 244), which is intentional for declined idle flushes.

Security-relevant observations:
(1) T-028: releaseRetained and the clearCache paths affect residual KV/GPU memory retention. Retaining the buffer pool while busy and flushing only when idle or under pressure is a modest change to residual-data lifetime. It is not a new disclosure path, because the operator already controls the process boundary (T-011, T-014). Host-zeroed segments are dropped on release.
(2) The idle sweep uses serviceBudget.isIdle/performIfIdle. If idleness is mis-tracked, the flush could be deferred. That is an availability and memory-pressure concern (T-029), and the pressure window still forces a flush when remainingBytes < pool + threshold.
(3) capacityShortfall uses checked arithmetic and saturates to .max on overflow. It subtracts via Self.subtract, whose behavior was not shown in the supplied excerpt; it is presumably saturating given how it is used.
(4) Unverified contracts: CBv2RetainedKVSegments.requestRelease and retainedBytes, EngineV2Factory.segmentRetentionEnabled, WholeMacServiceBudget, and the callers of capacityShortfall were not in the supplied evidence.
(5) T-041: the encrypted prefix cache and its TTL/HMAC controls are not modified. The changes do not touch the SSD cache, the key chain, or the staging reservations.

No concrete security regression was identified.
